page: Amazon Web Services i7i.8xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is driven by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores operating at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz. The CPU subsystem includes an extensive cache hierarchy, highlighted by a large 320 MB L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and AES-NI.

Memory configuration includes 256.0 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 RAM, equating to an 8.0 GB RAM-to-core allocation. Storage is anchored by 7,500 GB of attached local NVMe SSD capacity, providing direct low-latency disk access for data-heavy operations. The instance also features a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps, facilitating rapid inter-node replication and outbound transfers without standalone public IPv4 allocations included by default.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-core Geekbench scores and strong multi-core processing in both Geekbench and PassMark suites. The memory subsystem demonstrates strong uncached large-block read (206.98 GB/sec) and write (115.53 GB/sec) throughput, aiding compression and decompression tasks. Although small-scale LLM prompt processing and text generation perform strongly via CPU AMX extensions, text generation throughput falls into lower brackets on 70B parameter models due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware.

This server architecture balances compute power, memory density, and substantial integrated NVMe disk resources. It is well structured for high-IOPS relational databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, real-time analytics, and data-intensive caching layers that demand low disk latency alongside high memory bandwidth.
description: Amazon Web Services i7i.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with a 320 MB L3 cache and AMX acceleration. The platform includes 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz, combined with 7,500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core performance alongside strong multi-core computation and high uncached memory transfer rates. While suited for lightweight matrix operations and CPU-based LLM inference on small models, the instance lacks discrete GPUs, leading to diminished execution speeds on larger language models. The i7i.8xlarge provides a balanced hardware profile for storage-heavy enterprise workloads, transactional databases, and search clusters needing rapid local IOPS.
